headline_verdict: AT THE 18,000 DOLLAR ASK THE CONSERVATIVE CASE DOES NOT CLEAR. It clears under most-likely and aggressive assumptions only. The recommended ask is therefore smaller, and it is priced as decision data that gates the bigger spend.
cost_note: Five-year total cost of ownership, not sticker price, per Gartner TCO and the Forrester TEI four-part frame. Implementation is the 18,000 dollar fixed-price phase one ask exactly as sized in the economics pre-check, and it is not adjusted upward anywhere in this model. Training and change management is stated in HOURS and is entirely their people's time, about 84 hours in year one at the conservative population: 24 hours for an internal policy owner adjudicating the corpus contradictions and signing off one dated canonical source, 16 hours for operations to assemble and sign the vessel-to-departure map, about 11 hours to run the paper tally sheet for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season at roughly 10 minutes a shift, about 9 hours of cohort onboarding at 1.5 hours per first-season desk agent, and 24 hours of miss-log labelling by a named internal authority. Those hours are priced at assumed loaded rates and carried as a cost, never netted against the benefit. Ongoing run cost is real even though the funded build has no model in it and therefore has ZERO inference and ZERO token cost: it is the pre-season regression re-run and content refresh before March 7 each season, hosting and tooling, and the policy owner's review cadence, which the season-scoping problem makes annual and non-optional because two seasons are live at once on their own site today. Run cost accrues for 4.5 of the 5 years on a mid-year go-live convention. Contingency is 20 percent in the conservative case, 18 percent most-likely, 15 percent aggressive, at the top of the 15 to 20 band where the risk is organizational rather than technical, which is what it is here: the tally sheet, the corpus owner and the vessel map are all their work, not ours.

benefits.benefit: First-season desk agent hours lost finding a policy answer in weeks one through six
benefits.basis: Assumed 12 to 30 hours per first-season desk agent over weeks one to six, at an assumed loaded seasonal rate of 26 to 34 dollars an hour, times an assumed 6 to 15 first-season desk agents a year, times an assumed 25 to 55 percent of those hours removed. NO measured baseline exists. Median time to answer is recorded nowhere at this company today.
benefits.note: CAPACITY, not cash, and the redeploy / defer-hire / avoid-backfill test FAILS on two of three routes. Nobody gets un-hired: the cohort is hired in a fixed January 15th to April 15th window for a fixed March 7th to October 11th season, so there is no hire to defer and no backfill to avoid. Redeploy is the only honest route and it is partial, the freed hours go back into a shift the agent is already being paid for. A CFO should read this line as capacity created inside an already-committed payroll, never as a payroll reduction.

benefits.benefit: Veteran and supervisor hours consumed answering a first-season agent in weeks one through six
benefits.basis: Assumed 4 to 11 veteran hours consumed per first-season agent over weeks one to six, at an assumed loaded rate of 42 to 58 dollars an hour, times the same assumed 6 to 15 first-season agents, times an assumed 30 to 60 percent removed. Escalation rate is recorded nowhere today.
benefits.note: CAPACITY. Same failed test as the line above. This is the stronger of the two ramp lines on mechanism, because the interrupted person is a scarce one, and the strongest available evidence (i1, 5,179 agents) concentrates its effect on novices with near zero effect on experienced workers, which is exactly this shape. The second-order cost, a shoreside supervisor pulled off a boarding of up to 192 passengers to answer a refund clock question at 11:20 a.m., is REAL and is deliberately QUARANTINED as qualitative because it has no defensible denominator.

benefits.benefit: Refund paid on the wrong clock in the generous direction
benefits.basis: Assumed 6 to 26 events a season at an assumed 298 to 618 dollars an event, times an assumed 50 to 85 percent reduction. Cost per event is built ONLY from verified adult fares, two adults at 149 dollars conservative, two at 239 most-likely, two at 309 aggressive. Event frequency is a pure assumption with LOW confidence and it is the single driver that moves this whole analysis.
benefits.note: CASH, and the only line in the stack that needs no redeploy test, because it is money that leaves the bank account and does not come back. The mechanism is verified from their own published policy: three different refund clocks live on one page, 72 hours cruise-only, 7 days hotel package, 21 days transportation package. A first-season agent who quotes the headline 72-hour clock to a guest holding a 21-day transportation package refunds money the company did not owe, on a booking whose third-party transportation it may already be committed to. The transportation component of that refund is UNPUBLISHED and is excluded entirely from cost per event, which understates this line in all three scenarios.

benefits.benefit: Retrieval option never invoiced because the measured gate failed
benefits.basis: Assumed 22,000 to 38,000 dollars of gated build spend, times an assumed 35 to 60 percent probability that the three-part gate FAILS on measured evidence, entered as 0.22 to 0.23 events a year so that the one-time decision annualizes to almost exactly one occurrence across the five-year horizon.
benefits.note: CASH, avoided outflow. This is the pilot-as-decision-data line the run contract explicitly permits, and it is stated in those terms rather than dressed as an operational saving. The gate is numeric and can fail: at least 15 percent of logged questions falling outside the table, AND at least 20 distinct question types recurring three or more times, AND at least 150 labelled items after de-duplication. On a desk this small that is a demanding bar, and if the log lands under it the written outcome is that this business needed a rule set and not an AI, we say so, we do not invoice. The avoided RUN cost of the option that never gets built is deliberately excluded, which understates this line. Conservative here means a LOW probability of the gate failing, because a failing gate is what produces the benefit.

benefits.benefit: Pre-season policy reconciliation across the website, two hotel front desks and the dock
benefits.basis: Assumed 900 to 2,600 dollars a year of current ad-hoc reconciliation effort, times an assumed 40 to 65 percent removed by one dated canonical source. The reduction is stated NET of the maintenance hours already carried in run cost, so it is not double counted.
benefits.note: CAPACITY, a retained asset with recurring value rather than a cash saving. The defect rate behind it is verified rather than assumed: two of their own pages give different parking prices, a live 2026 booking page still carries 2020 and 2021 copy, the FAQ names a vessel running a scheduled 12:30 pm departure that the eight-vessel fleet page does not list, and a product with a live 2026 page is missing from the five-product index. It recurs annually by construction because two seasons are live at once on their site right now, the 4 Hour at 149 dollars for 2026 and the Spring Wildlife at 109 dollars for 2027.

benefit_lines_labelled.label: CAPACITY
benefit_lines_labelled.defer_hire: FAILS, the cohort is hired in a fixed window for a fixed season
benefit_lines_labelled.avoid_backfill: FAILS, there is no backfill in a seasonal rebuild
benefit_lines_labelled.redeploy: PARTIAL, hours return to a shift already paid for
benefit_lines_labelled.verdict: Capacity created inside committed payroll. Not a payroll reduction and the study must not imply one.

benefit_lines_labelled.label: CAPACITY
benefit_lines_labelled.redeploy: YES, into peak-season shoreside operations, which is where the scarcity actually is
benefit_lines_labelled.verdict: Capacity created, with the clearest redeploy route of the two ramp lines. Still not cash.

benefit_lines_labelled.line: Refund paid on the wrong clock in the generous direction
benefit_lines_labelled.label: CASH
benefit_lines_labelled.verdict: Avoided cash outflow. Money that leaves the account and does not return. The only unambiguous cash line built on operations rather than on a purchasing decision.

benefit_lines_labelled.line: Retrieval option never invoiced because the gate failed
benefit_lines_labelled.label: CASH
benefit_lines_labelled.verdict: Avoided capital outflow on a build that the evidence says should not happen. Honest only because the gate is numeric, is written before the work starts, and can fail against us.

benefit_lines_labelled.label: CAPACITY
benefit_lines_labelled.verdict: Capacity plus a retained asset. Counted at a haircut and net of the maintenance hours already sitting in run cost.

quarantined_qualitative_benefits: A shoreside supervisor not pulled off a boarding to answer a policy question at the moment a cruise is loading. Real, and it has no denominator, so it stays out of the formula.

The strict-direction refund error, where a guest is refused a refund they were entitled to under the published policy. This is NOT a cash benefit, the company keeps that money. It is a reputation cost on a thirty-year locally owned family brand whose competitive position against a NYSE-listed operator in the same harbour is exactly that. It stays out of the formula.

The accessibility branch. Telling a wheelchair user a departure is accessible when the vessel running it is not has the highest cost of error in the business and the only dignity dimension, and it is the one error with no catcher upstream of the dock. It is excluded from the formula because it depends on a vessel-to-departure map that does not exist yet, and because assuming the company writes a discretionary refund is an assumption about behaviour we can't verify.

A wrong shuttle answer that causes a missed sailing. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED AND IT MUST STAY EXCLUDED. Their published policy makes a no-show completely non-refundable, so the company KEEPS that fare. The cost is goodwill and reputation, not revenue, and counting it as revenue would be dishonest.

The change-fee line, a 15 dollar per person re-booking fee forgone when a novice quotes a free date change to a guest already on their second change. Verified, real, and immaterial. Dropped on purpose rather than stacked, because a weak line makes the whole case weaker.
benefit_phasing: No day-one benefit anywhere in this model. The funded build lands in the March 2027 cohort's hands, so YEAR ONE IS ONE SEASON AND NOT TWELVE MONTHS OF STEADY STATE, and the season itself is March 7th to October 11th rather than a calendar year. Year one is discounted to 30 percent of run rate conservative, 45 percent most-likely, 60 percent aggressive, and that discount is ADOPTION, not calendar: a brand-new lookup in the hands of a cohort that is itself brand new, with the corpus owner still settling contradictions mid-season and the table covering four branches out of everything the desk gets asked. Years two through five run at full rate, which is the right shape here rather than an optimistic one, because the population resets every spring by the company's own published hiring pattern, so the tool meets a fresh novice cohort every March instead of decaying into a habit nobody uses. Compounding is real on the retained assets and is NOT modelled, the canonical policy source and the vessel map get better each season they are maintained and we take no credit for that. The recommended smaller ask ramps faster, 70 percent in year one, because the paper tally sheet starts in the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and the canonical source is usable the day it is signed off.

scenarios.conservative: 6 first-season desk agents, 12 novice hours and 4 veteran hours each over weeks one to six, 25 and 30 percent of those hours removed, 6 wrong-clock refunds a season at two adults on the lowest verified fare, 50 percent of them prevented, a 22,000 dollar gated option with a 35 percent chance the gate fails, 20 percent contingency, 30 percent year-one ramp. THIS CASE DOES NOT CLEAR AT 18,000. It recovers roughly a third of five-year TCO and we expect roi_math.py to return no payback inside the horizon.
scenarios.most_likely: 10 first-season desk agents, 20 novice hours and 7 veteran hours each, 40 and 45 percent removed, 14 wrong-clock refunds a season at two adults on the 6 Hour fare, 70 percent prevented, a 30,000 dollar gated option at a 50 percent chance of failing, 18 percent contingency, 45 percent year-one ramp. This case clears, and it clears thinly, with payback deep in year four. A thin most-likely case is not a strong buy signal and we are not going to call it one.
scenarios.aggressive: 15 first-season desk agents, 30 novice hours and 11 veteran hours each, 55 and 60 percent removed, 26 wrong-clock refunds a season at two adults on the highest verified fare, 85 percent prevented, a 38,000 dollar gated option at a 60 percent chance of failing, 15 percent contingency, 60 percent year-one ramp. This case clears comfortably and it rests almost entirely on an error frequency nobody has ever counted. The spread between conservative and aggressive is more than tenfold, which is the honest signature of a case with no baseline.
scenarios.recommended_ask_conservative: The SAME conservative benefit assumptions applied to a 4,500 dollar Phase Zero with no software in it. This case clears, at the margin, and it is the only version of this engagement whose conservative case clears.

conservative_clears_reasoning: At the 18,000 dollar ask, no. We are saying that in the heading rather than in a footnote, as the economics pre-check required. The quantifiable annual benefit under conservative assumptions lands in the low thousands, the five-year TCO at 18,000 lands near 50,000 once training hours, five years of run cost and 20 percent contingency are in it, and roughly a third of that gets recovered. The verdict is robust: we re-tested it against higher agent counts, a larger cost per refund error and a doubled event frequency, and conservative still fails. It fails for a reason that is a fact about the business rather than a fact about the build, the desk is small and its headcount is unpublished, which is exactly what the conscience gate said before this analysis started. The RECOMMENDED ASK is therefore not 18,000 today. It is about 4,500 dollars for a Phase Zero with no software in it, and the conservative case for that one clears. We want to be blunt about how that 4,500 was arrived at, because a CFO is entitled to suspect it: it is not a bottom-up scope estimate that happened to clear, it is the CEILING the conservative benefit supports, solved for, and the scope was then cut to fit under it. Saying that out loud is the point. Phase Zero is the corpus crawl and the conflict list, facilitated adjudication with a named internal owner producing one dated canonical policy source, the vessel-map workshop with a written abstain rule, the paper tally sheet installed for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season, and the miss-log specification including the PII rule, the held-out split and the supervisor sampling arm. The 18,000 dollar decision table is not withdrawn, it is RE-PRICED against a measured baseline in autumn 2027, when the tally sheet has produced the denominator this analysis did not have. If the counted error frequency lands anywhere near the most-likely assumption, the 18,000 dollar build clears conservatively at that point and we will show the arithmetic again with real numbers in it.
payback_range: Reported as a range and never as a point, and every month figure is computed by scripts/roi_math.py rather than narrated here. At the 18,000 dollar ask we expect the range to run from NO PAYBACK INSIDE FIVE YEARS in the conservative case, through payback deep in year four most-likely, to somewhere in year two aggressive. At the recommended 4,500 dollar Phase Zero ask we expect conservative payback near the end of the five-year horizon, which is honest rather than attractive, and which is why the case for Phase Zero rests on the decision it buys rather than on its payback speed. Two calendar adjustments the reader must apply and which the script does not model. First, month zero is GO-LIVE, so the four-month build and reconciliation period that precedes March 2027 sits before month one and pushes every calendar date out by about four months. Second, benefit only accrues while a season runs, March 7th to October 11th, so a payback month is a position on a benefit curve that is flat for roughly five months of every year. Where this section and the script disagree, THE SCRIPT WINS and this sentence is the defect.
base_rate_note: The outside view first, stated at full strength rather than as a hedge. MIT's finding is that about 95 percent of generative AI pilots produce no measurable P&L impact. RAND puts AI project failure at about 80 percent, roughly double the rate for non-AI IT projects. Reference-class forecasting says the right prior for this build is that it does nothing, and an inside-view estimate written by the people who would be paid to do the work is exactly the estimate that prior exists to correct. Six specific things put this build in the small share that pays, and the first one is the strongest. ONE, THE FUNDED SCOPE CONTAINS NO MODEL. It is a deterministic decision table over a finite, already-published input space, so the dominant failure mode in that 95 percent, a probabilistic system whose real-world error rate nobody measured, is absent by construction rather than managed. TWO, the acceptance bar is 100 percent agreement across an EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION of the input cross product, certified rather than sampled. Almost nothing in AI can be certified, and this can. THREE, it FAILS CLOSED. Any input combination not in the table returns no published rule for this case, escalate to the named role, and writes a miss-log entry. It never interpolates and never guesses, and the accessibility branch abstains outright whenever the vessel serving a departure is not known with certainty. FOUR, it is aimed at the population where the strongest available evidence concentrates its effect, novices, with near zero effect on experienced workers, and it deliberately does not target the 22-year vice president or the 15-year maintenance director. A rollout to everyone would dilute into an average that looks like failure while the tool worked exactly as measured. FIVE, the baseline is a NAMED DELIVERABLE rather than an assumption, so the variance check can actually run, and a case that plans to be checked is the marker the failure literature keeps identifying. SIX, the next spend is gated on a number that can fail against us and we have written down that we do not invoice if it fails. Now the counterweight, which belongs in the same paragraph rather than in a softer one further down. Design does not beat a base rate on its own, execution does, and the single largest risk here is not technical at all. It is that nobody at Major Marine runs a paper tally for nine weeks. If that happens the outcome is unmeasurable, and unmeasurable is not a smaller claim, it is a different kind of claim, and the study says so rather than promising a measured result.
value_owner: PROPOSED, and they assign it, we do not. The number should sit with ONE named person on their side and we propose the Director of Shoreside Operations, Kirsten McNeil, at 11 years, because the check-in office and the reservations desk are inside that remit and because a value owner who does not control the workflow cannot move the number. Two supporting owners, each named because the analysis fails without them. The Operations Manager, Tayja Wright, at 8 years, runs the paper tally sheet for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and re-runs it in the same calendar weeks of 2027, which is the entire measurement apparatus. A named internal POLICY owner adjudicates every corpus contradiction and signs the one dated canonical source, and we propose the Director of Sales, Kori Goertz, because pricing and package rules sit in that role, and because only somebody inside the company knows which parking price is the right one. That last role is not optional and it is not ours to fill. Alaska AI owns the build and the arithmetic. Alaska AI does not own the adoption, and pretending otherwise is how the 95 percent gets made.
variance_check: Baseline first, because there isn't one today. The paper tally sheet runs from now to October 11th, 2026, the final nine weeks of the season, recording question asked, time to answer, escalated or not, and to whom. Zero software and zero cost. It is re-run in the SAME CALENDAR WEEKS of 2027 so the comparison is season-matched rather than calendar-matched, which matters on an operation whose volume is shaped entirely by the season. Four checks at that point. ONE, the three operational metrics, median time to answer, escalation rate for first-season agents, and count of policy misquotes reaching a guest, all three of which must fall with no fall in guest experience. TWO, the cash check, counted generous-direction refund errors in 2027 against the 2026 tally, reported whether it moved or not, and this is the check that decides whether the 18,000 dollar build is ever worth buying. THREE, the miss log counted against all three parts of the gate, 15 percent outside the table, 20 distinct types recurring three or more times, 150 labelled items after de-duplication, published as a result either way. FOUR, a re-run of this exact ROI model with the counted numbers substituted for the assumed ones, with every driver that moved named and the direction it moved in. One guard against ourselves, written down now rather than later. The party that designs the table is the party that determines what counts as a miss, and a narrower table produces a fatter miss log. The table's boundaries are therefore agreed with the client UP FRONT, and the supervisor logs every question on two randomly chosen full days a month so the log has an arm that is not selected by us or by a busy agent.
what_would_make_this_wrong: THE TALLY SHEET NEVER RUNS. This is the largest risk in the whole case and it is not a technical one. Every driver in this model is an assumption, the tally sheet is the only thing that converts any of them into a measurement, and it is their work rather than ours. If it does not run, the honest position is that the outcome can't be measured, and we say so instead of promising a measured result.

THE REFUND ERROR FREQUENCY IS LOWER THAN 6 A SEASON. That single driver moves this analysis more than any other. If the desk almost never quotes the wrong clock, the cash strand collapses, the whole case rests on capacity hours that are not payroll reductions, and the correct answer is that they should not buy the decision table at any price. We would rather find that in September 2026 than in March 2027.

THE DESK SHARE OF THE 60 SEASONAL HIRES IS SMALLER THAN ASSUMED. About 60 seasonal employees is verified from their own employment page. The share who work the reservations desk is UNPUBLISHED, and we assumed 10 to 25 percent. Deckhands, cooks, engineering and dock support are the bulk of a boat operation. If the desk is three people and two of them return every year, both ramp lines shrink toward nothing.

THE VESSEL-TO-DEPARTURE MAP TURNS OUT NOT TO BE STABLE. If vessel assignment moves with maintenance and charters, the accessibility branch never ships, the table covers three branches rather than four, and every cut percentage in the ramp lines is too high.

THE LOADED HOURLY RATES ARE WRONG. Nothing about their pay is published. We assumed 26 to 34 dollars loaded for a seasonal agent and 42 to 58 for a veteran or supervisor, built up from an assumed wage plus payroll burden plus the real employer-side cost implied by their own published housing and travel support. If the true loaded rate is lower, both capacity lines shrink proportionally.

THE CAPACITY LINES GET READ AS CASH. They are not cash and we have labelled them capacity in every place they appear. If a reader mentally converts freed hours into a smaller payroll, the case looks roughly twice as good as it is. On a fixed seasonal cohort hired inside a fixed window, that conversion is simply not available.

THE GATED OPTION IS PRICED WRONG. The 22,000 to 38,000 dollar range for the retrieval option is our own assumed scope rather than a quote, and we chose to use our own number precisely because a vendor average would be worthless as this company's baseline. If that option would really cost far less, the decision-data line shrinks and the recommended Phase Zero ask stops clearing.

WE PRICED PHASE ZERO BY SOLVING FOR THE CEILING. The 4,500 dollar figure is the largest ask the conservative benefit supports, solved for, with the scope then cut to fit under it. That is a legitimate way to size an ask and it is also exactly the move Flyvbjerg warns about, so it is disclosed here rather than presented as a coincidence. If the scope cannot honestly be delivered for 4,500, the ask does not go up, the recommendation becomes the free tally sheet alone.
assumptions: NO BASELINE EXISTS. Median time to answer, escalation rate and policy-misquote count are recorded nowhere at this company today. Reservations desk headcount, annual passenger volume and call volume are all unpublished. Every driver below is a STATED ASSUMPTION and not a measurement, and no hours-saved case is built on an unpublished headcount denominator anywhere in this model.

pursuits_per_year, meaning first-season desk agents a year, assumed at 6 conservative, 10 most-likely, 15 aggressive. Chosen as roughly 10, 17 and 25 percent of the verified about 60 seasonal employees, on the assumption that Customer Service and Sales Staff, which their own employment page lists first among six role categories, covers the phone desk plus the check-in office plus the dock ticket window, and on the further assumption that most of that group is new each spring given a hiring window of January 15th to April 15th. Confidence LOW on the split, MODERATE on the annual rebuild.

hours_per_pursuit on the novice line, assumed 12 conservative, 20 most-likely, 30 aggressive, over weeks one to six. Built from an assumed 20 questions per agent per day across roughly 30 shifts, with an assumed extra 2 to 4 minutes per lookup on the share of questions that need a policy page. Confidence LOW.

hours_per_pursuit on the veteran line, assumed 4 conservative, 7 most-likely, 11 aggressive, of veteran time consumed per first-season agent over the same six weeks. Chosen at roughly a third of the novice figure on the assumption that most lookups are self-served and only the harder ones escalate. Confidence LOW.

rate on the novice line, assumed 26, 30 and 34 dollars an hour fully loaded. Built from an assumed base wage plus assumed payroll burden plus the real employer-side cost implied by their own published employee housing from 15 dollars a night and a 400 dollar out-of-state travel reimbursement, whose magnitude is unpublished. Confidence LOW. This is an assumption, never a fact, and it is not an industry average.

rate on the veteran line, assumed 42, 50 and 58 dollars an hour fully loaded for a returning senior agent, supervisor or manager. Confidence LOW, chosen deliberately below what a director-level interruption is actually worth so the line cannot be accused of inflation.

cut on the novice line, assumed 0.25, 0.40 and 0.55, and on the veteran line 0.30, 0.45 and 0.60. Bounded well under 1.0 because the funded table covers only four branches out of everything the desk is asked, and because the veteran line has the cleaner mechanism, a lookup removes the go-ask-somebody step more completely than it removes reading time. Confidence LOW.

events_per_year on the refund line, assumed 6 conservative, 14 most-likely, 26 aggressive. THIS IS THE DRIVER THAT MOVES THE ANSWER and it has no denominator, because booking volume is unpublished. 6 a season is roughly one every five weeks of a 31-week season, chosen as a floor rather than a middle. Confidence VERY LOW and stated as such wherever this number appears.

cost_per_event on the refund line, assumed 298, 478 and 618 dollars, constructed identically across all three scenarios as TWO ADULTS at a verified adult fare, 149 dollars on the 4 Hour conservative, 239 on the 6 Hour most-likely, 309 on the 8.5 Hour aggressive. Party size of two is assumed. The transportation component of a transportation package is UNPUBLISHED and is excluded entirely, which understates all three figures. Confidence MODERATE on the fares because they are verified, LOW on party size.

reduction on the refund line, assumed 0.50, 0.70 and 0.85. Bounded by ADOPTION rather than by tool accuracy, because the table itself is certified at 100 percent agreement across an exhaustive enumeration and the refund branch has no abstain path, its inputs are booking contents the agent enters by hand. Confidence MODERATE.

cost_per_event on the decision-data line, assumed 22,000, 30,000 and 38,000 dollars for the gated snippet-retrieval option. This is OUR OWN assumed scope, used deliberately in place of any vendor or industry figure. It excludes the multi-year run cost of the option that never gets built, which understates the line. Confidence LOW.

reduction on the decision-data line, meaning the probability the three-part gate FAILS on measured evidence, assumed 0.35, 0.50 and 0.60. Conservative here means a LOW probability, because a failing gate is what creates the benefit. There is a real argument that 0.35 is too low, since 150 labelled items after de-duplication is a demanding bar on a small desk and under-logging at peak is guaranteed, and we left it low on purpose. Confidence LOW.

events_per_year on the decision-data line, set at 0.23 conservative and 0.22 in the other cases. This is a MODELLING CONVENTION, not a frequency. The decision is a one-time event at the end of the 2027 season, and 0.22 to 0.23 a year annualizes to almost exactly one occurrence across the five-year horizon under each scenario's ramp multiplier. It is disclosed here because a reader who took it literally would be misled.

The reconciliation line, assumed 900, 1,600 and 2,600 dollars a year of current ad-hoc effort at an assumed 45 dollar loaded rate, times an assumed 0.40, 0.55 and 0.65 removed. The reduction is stated NET of the maintenance hours already carried inside run cost, so the same work is not counted on both sides of the ledger. The underlying defect rate is verified rather than assumed, four independent freshness and consistency defects found in one afternoon of external reading of a corpus of roughly thirty pages. Confidence MODERATE on the defects, LOW on the effort figure.

implementation set at 18,000 dollars in all three scenarios, exactly the fixed-price phase one ask from the economics pre-check, never adjusted upward anywhere in this model. The fourth scenario sets it at 4,500 for the recommended Phase Zero.

training set at 3,500, 4,600 and 6,200 dollars, which is entirely THEIR hours and not an invoice. About 84 hours in year one at the conservative population, itemised in cost_note. It rises in the aggressive case because a larger desk means more onboarding and more labelling, which keeps the scenarios internally consistent rather than letting the aggressive case get cheaper as it gets bigger.

run_cost_per_year set at 4,800, 3,600 and 2,800 dollars, and 1,000 for the recommended Phase Zero. There is ZERO inference cost and ZERO token cost because the funded build has no model in it. What remains is the pre-season regression re-run and content refresh before March 7th each season, hosting and tooling, and the policy owner's review cadence. Season scoping makes the refresh annual and non-optional, because two seasons are live at once. Confidence MODERATE.
run_cost_years set at 4.5 of the 5-year horizon in every scenario, the mid-year go-live convention used by scripts/roi_math.py.

contingency set at 0.20 conservative, 0.18 most-likely, 0.15 aggressive, inside the 15 to 20 percent band. Top of the band conservative because the failure risk here is organizational rather than technical, the tally sheet and the corpus owner and the vessel map are all their work.

year1_ramp set at 0.30, 0.45 and 0.60, and 0.70 for the recommended Phase Zero. This is ADOPTION and not calendar. The build lands with the March 2027 cohort so year one contains one full season, and the discount reflects a new tool in the hands of a new cohort with the corpus owner still settling contradictions mid-season. Phase Zero ramps faster because the paper tally sheet starts in the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and the canonical source is usable on sign-off.
years set at 5 in every scenario, per the Gartner five-year TCO horizon.
The change-fee benefit, a 15 dollar per person re-booking fee forgone, is EXCLUDED on purpose despite being verified, because it is immaterial and a weak fifth line makes the whole stack weaker.

The staff-engineer design and product-manager metrics files were not on disk at the time this analysis was written. It is built on claims.json, the locked pick with its economics pre-check, and the conscience gate's feasibility file, and every driver above should be re-checked against the design and the PRD before the study ships.
tco_notes: Four notes for whoever runs the arithmetic. ONE, the drivers object below carries FOUR scenarios, not three. The first three all sit at the 18,000 dollar ask so the reader sees that ask evaluated honestly under every assumption set. The fourth, recommended_ask_conservative, applies the SAME conservative benefit assumptions to the smaller Phase Zero ask, and it exists because the role requires the recommended ask to be one whose conservative case clears, and because saying what ask size it clears at is only auditable if the drivers are on the table. scripts/roi_math.py iterates over whatever keys are in scenarios, so all four compute. TWO, every derived figure comes from that script and none of it is narrated here. Where a sentence in this file and the script output disagree, the script wins and the sentence is the defect. THREE, the payback month the script returns is measured from GO-LIVE, so the four-month build and reconciliation period before March 2027 sits before month one and every calendar date moves out by about four months. Both adjustments are stated rather than modelled. FOUR, no single hero number appears anywhere in this file and none should appear in the study. The conservative case at 18,000 does not clear, and that sentence belongs in the ROI section's heading per FIELD_STUDY_SPEC, not in a footnote.
